summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes, chronic systolic heart failure, and bilateral below-knee amputations was admitted for acute renal failure and hyperkalemia discovered during a clinic visit. She was treated for a urinary tract infection caused by Citrobacter freundii, initially with meropenem and later switched to ciprofloxacin based on culture results. Her hyperkalemia resolved with medical management, and her renal function improved with hydration and antibiotics. Due to recurrent UTIs and incomplete bladder emptying, a Foley catheter was placed, and she was referred to urology for clean intermittent catheterization training. She underwent a right BKA revision for a nonhealing ulcer, which healed well. Medication adjustments included increasing metoprolol, starting lisinopril, stopping fluconazole, and reducing vancomycin dose. She was discharged home with nursing services, stable and afebrile, with follow-up arranged across multiple specialties.
